newsitem.title: USA: Sun Television to be acquired by Gregg Appliances.
newsitem.headline: Sun Television to be acquired by Gregg Appliances.

text.p: Sun Television & Appliances, Inc. said Wednesday it has agreed to be acquired by Gregg Appliances, Inc., another appliance and electronics retailer, for about $87 million in cash.
Under the agreement, Sun shareholders will receive $5.00 in cash for each of Sun's roughly 17.4 million common shares.

Sun shareholders will also receive estimated net proceeds of about 90 cents to $1.25 per share from expected tax refunds for income taxes paid by Sun during fiscal 1994-1996, resulting from tax loss carrybacks generated by the merger.
The deal is expected to close before Feb. 28, subject to due diligence, negotiation of a definitive merger agreement and approval of Sun shareholders and regulators.

Sun also it will refinance the company's unsecured $30 million senior notes and $50 million revolving bank debt by year's end. The company has received a commitment letter from the CIT Group/Business Credit, Inc. for $100 million of three-year secured revolving bank debt.
Gregg, a privately held company based in Indianapolis, operates 18 H.H. Gregg Appliances & Electronics stores in Indiana, Kentucky and Tennessee.
Sun, based in Columbus, Ohio, operates 50 stores in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia and Kentucky.
Sun's stock rose 50 cents to $4.625 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
